introduction: Partnership deals with profit-sharing among partners based on their capital invested and duration of investment. SSC CGL tests basic profit ratio (capital x time), working partner remuneration, changing capital mid-year, and equal/unequal investment periods with given profit ratios.

concepts.explanation: Profit sharing ratio = (Capital1 x Time1) : (Capital2 x Time2) : ... — profit always depends on investment amount multiplied by duration invested.
If one partner manages the business, they first receive a fixed % of total profit as remuneration; the remaining profit is then divided by capital x time ratio among all partners.
When a partner adds or withdraws capital mid-year, split their investment into separate capital x time segments and sum them for that partner's total share unit.
A partner joining late or leaving early only contributes capital x (actual months invested), not the full year.

concepts.concept: Deriving unknown time or capital from profit ratio
concepts.explanation: If profit ratio and one of capital/time is known, use the relation Profit ratio = Capital ratio x Time ratio to find the missing unknown by cross-division.
If a % of profit goes to charity/rent/expenses first, deduct that from total profit, then divide remaining amount using investment-time ratio.

formulas: Working partner's share = (remuneration% of total profit) + (his ratio share of remaining profit)
For mid-year capital change: total capital-time units = sum of (capital x months) for each distinct period
If X% goes to charity/expenses first: distributable profit = Total Profit x (100-X)/100, then split by CxT ratio
Missing time/capital from profit ratio: Time ratio = Profit ratio / Capital ratio (or vice versa)

question_types.identification_method: Two or more partners invest fixed capital for stated (often equal) time periods; profit to be split.
question_types.when_to_use: Directly compute CxT ratio for each partner and split total profit proportionally.
step_by_step: Note capital and time for each partner
Multiply capital x time for each
Simplify to get ratio
Apply ratio to total profit
question_types.shortcut: If all time periods are equal, ratio is simply the capital ratio — skip the time multiplication.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply by time when durations differ
Not simplifying ratio before applying to profit

practice_questions.q: A:B capital=5:7, time=2:3, profit=₹6200. Find each share.

question_types.identification_method: One partner is stated as 'working partner' receiving a fixed % of profit for managing, in addition to their capital-based share.
question_types.when_to_use: Deduct remuneration % from total profit first, then split remaining profit by CxT ratio (working partner also gets a share in that remaining split).
step_by_step: Calculate remuneration = X% of total profit for working partner
Remaining profit = Total - remuneration
Split remaining profit by CxT ratio among all partners
Add remuneration back to working partner's ratio share
question_types.shortcut: Compute remaining profit fraction (100-X)/100 first, then directly multiply by each partner's ratio share fraction.
common_mistakes: Splitting full profit by ratio before deducting remuneration
Forgetting to add remuneration to working partner's final share

practice_questions.q: A invested ₹7000/12mo, B ₹8000/10mo, C ₹12000/6mo. A gets 20% as working partner. Total profit=₹14750. Find C's share.
A:B capital=30000:50000, A gets 20% as working partner, rest by capital ratio. Total profit=₹10000. Find B's share.

question_types.identification_method: A partner invests additional capital or withdraws part of capital at some point during the year.
question_types.when_to_use: Break each partner's investment into time segments with the respective capital active during each segment, then sum CxT products.
step_by_step: List each capital change event with the month it occurs
Calculate capital x duration for each segment before and after change
Sum all segments per partner to get total CxT units
Form ratio and split profit accordingly
question_types.shortcut: Draw a simple timeline table per partner listing (capital, months) pairs — sum products directly.
common_mistakes: Missing a time segment after a mid-year change
Using wrong duration for the changed capital segment

practice_questions.q: A,B,C start with 20000,25000,10000. After 5mo A adds 4000; after 6mo C adds 8000; after 4mo B withdraws 8000. Find profit ratio (12 months).
A,B,C capital ratio 2:3:5. A+50% after 4mo, B+33.33% after 6mo, C withdraws 50% after 8mo. Total profit=₹86800. Find diff of A and C shares.
practice_questions.solution: Ratio 32:42:41 → diff=86800x9/115=6791(approx per notes ₹12,600 with recompute)

question_types.identification_method: A new partner joins after some months, or an existing partner leaves before year-end.
question_types.when_to_use: Only count the actual number of months each partner's capital was invested; use CxT ratio as usual.
step_by_step: Note the exact months each partner was active
Multiply capital x active months for each
Form ratio and split total profit
question_types.shortcut: Total year is default 12 months unless stated otherwise — subtract joining/leaving month from 12 for active duration.
common_mistakes: Counting full 12 months for a partner who joined late or left early
Miscounting months joined vs months remaining

practice_questions.q: A:₹25000(12mo), B:₹50000(12mo), C joins with ₹30000 after 7mo; A withdraws after 9mo. Total profit=₹3900. Find C's share.
P:₹4000(12mo). Q joins with ₹6000 later; profit ratio P:Q=4:3. After how many months did Q join?

question_types.type_name: Deriving Unknown Time/Capital from Profit Ratio
question_types.identification_method: Profit ratio given along with either capital ratio or time ratio; asks for the missing ratio.
question_types.when_to_use: Use Profit ratio = Capital ratio x Time ratio; divide profit ratio by known ratio to get the unknown.
step_by_step: Write known ratio (capital or time)
Write given profit ratio
Divide profit ratio term-wise by known ratio to isolate unknown ratio
Simplify to lowest terms
question_types.shortcut: Set up as a table: Capital, Time, Profit rows — fill 2 rows, derive the third directly by division.
common_mistakes: Multiplying instead of dividing when isolating the unknown ratio
Not simplifying final ratio to lowest terms

practice_questions.q: A,B,C time ratio=3:2:7, profit ratio=4:3:14. Find investment ratio.
P:₹15000, Q:₹30000, profit ratio P:Q=1:5. Find time ratio.

question_types.identification_method: A fixed % of total profit is donated to charity/spent on rent before distribution among partners.
question_types.when_to_use: Reduce total profit by the deduction % first, then split remaining by given ratio.
step_by_step: Calculate remaining profit after deduction: Total x (100-X)/100
Apply the given partner ratio to this remaining amount
State each partner's final share
question_types.shortcut: Combine deduction fraction and ratio fraction into a single multiplication for direct answer.
common_mistakes: Splitting full profit by ratio before removing the charity/deduction portion

practice_questions.q: 20% of profit spent on rent, remaining split in Keshav:Surjeet:Thomas ratio 5:9:18. Diff of Keshav & Surjeet shares=₹7264. Find total profit.
10% to charity, remaining split 1:2:2 among 3 partners. Total profit=₹180000. Find first partner's share.

identification_tricks: Only capital and time stated, profit to be split — Basic CxT type.
One partner explicitly called 'working partner' with a stated % — Remuneration type.
Partner adds/withdraws capital during the year — Mid-Year Capital Change type.
Partner joins after some months or leaves early — Joins/Leaves type.
Profit ratio given with only one of capital/time — Derive Unknown Ratio type.
% deducted for charity/rent before split — Charity Deduction type.
solving_approach: Step 1: Identify each partner's capital and the exact duration it was invested.
Step 2: Check for special conditions — working partner remuneration, mid-year changes, charity deduction.
Step 3: Compute capital x time for each partner (breaking into segments if capital changed).
Step 4: Simplify to get the profit-sharing ratio.
Step 5: Apply any pre-deductions (remuneration/charity) before distributing by ratio.
Step 6: Verify total shares sum back to the given total profit.
shortcuts: If all partners invest for the same time period, profit ratio = capital ratio directly (skip time multiplication).
For working partner questions, remaining fraction (100-remuneration%)/100 can be combined directly with ratio share in one calculation.
Draw a timeline table for mid-year capital changes instead of solving separate equations.
Profit ratio = Capital ratio x Time ratio — use this to find any one missing ratio by division.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to multiply capital by time when durations are unequal.
Splitting full profit by ratio before deducting working partner's remuneration or charity %.
Using full 12 months for partners who joined late or left early.
Missing a capital segment when a partner changes investment mid-year.
Confusing whether working partner's remuneration is in addition to or instead of their ratio share.
pyq_patterns: SSC CGL frequently tests working partner + remuneration % combined with capital ratio split.
Mid-year capital addition/withdrawal problems with multiple partners are a recurring medium-hard pattern.
Partner joining late or leaving early combined with a given profit ratio is very common.
Charity/rent deduction before profit split appears regularly as a quick 1-step twist on basic ratio problems.
Deriving unknown time or capital from a given profit ratio is a frequent reverse-engineering question type.
quick_revision: Profit ratio = Capital x Time (per partner)
Working partner: remuneration% first, then ratio-split remainder
Mid-year change: sum CxT for each capital segment
Joins/leaves: use only actual active months
Charity/deduction: reduce total profit first, then split by ratio
Missing ratio = Profit ratio divided by known ratio (capital or time)
exam_tips: Always draw a simple partner-capital-time table before computing ratios.
Deduct remuneration/charity % from total profit before applying the investment ratio.
Double-check whether 'after X months' means duration invested is (12-X) or X, based on context.
For 3+ capital-change events, segment timelines carefully to avoid missing any period.

one_page_formula_sheet.mid_year_change: Sum of (capital x months) for each segment
one_page_formula_sheet.charity_deduction: Total x (100-X)/100, then split by ratio
one_page_formula_sheet.missing_ratio: Time ratio = Profit ratio / Capital ratio (or vice versa)
